title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Tunnel Handler Dispatch Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, RFC 9220 parser regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers server-side dispatch of a validated websocket Extended CONNECT request to an application tunnel handler after sending a 200 response HEADERS frame without ending the stream. It also covers one bidirectional tunnel exchange using a masked client WebSocket text frame and an unmasked server text frame over the same request stream, plus the negative unsupported-protocol path when a WebSocket handler is configured.
preconditions: The RFC 9220 Extended CONNECT foundation remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0001`.
The WebSocket frame parser remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
expected_result: The focused loopback and parser tests pass, the new RFC 9220 handler requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server now has locally verified application handler dispatch for accepted RFC 9220 websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel streams. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
